workers.purpose: Create a consistent categorized procurement request that downstream sourcing, approval, and issuance activities can rely on.

input_contract.description: Original purchase request details.

input_contract.name: requested_item_or_service
input_contract.description: Description of the item or service being requested.

decisions.reason: This is a coherent normalization/classification job with explicit inputs and outputs that downstream sourcing, approval, and issuance steps depend on. It has a clear invocation point at the start of the reusable process, and its results can be bound directly into caller state as normalized_request and determined_procurement_category.

This candidate performs a distinct callable job: deriving an eligible vendor pool from the normalized request and eligibility context. Inputs are named, output is singular and useful, and it has a clear invocation point immediately after request normalization with straightforward handoff into subsequent sourcing.

Although delegation is explicitly allowed for bounded sourcing or quote-comparison subtasks, the candidate_kind is explicit_delegation rather than bounded_subtask, so it does not satisfy the required accepted boundary_kind match. The task itself has strong callable characteristics, but the candidate metadata needs repair before extraction under the required format.

This is a well-bounded evaluation job that consumes normalized sourcing artifacts and produces a promotability decision plus evaluation record. The process explicitly invokes this after sourcing, and the outputs bind directly into approval routing or rejection handling. It is more than a simple step because it consolidates budget, compliance, and eligibility determination into a reusable callable unit.

This candidate is explicitly an over-budget recovery path triggered only when evaluation fails budget limits. That makes it an alternative/failure path rather than an independently valuable callable boundary in the main decomposition.

This candidate handles non-compliance remediation, waiver, or restart behavior only when compliance failure occurs. It is therefore an alternative/exceptional flow governed by policy, not a primary independent worker boundary for the main process.

Approval routing is a coherent callable job with named inputs, a clear output contract, and an explicit invocation point after vendor selection/evaluation. The returned approval_record binds directly to issuance and audit steps. Despite being integration-oriented, it is broader than a single raw API call because it applies threshold/category routing rules to obtain the outcome.

This is the straightforward issuance step that follows once approvals and gates pass. While inputs and output are named, it functions as an ordinary terminal sequential step tightly coupled to the main flow rather than an independently valuable semantic boundary.

Archiving audit evidence is a discrete callable persistence job with clear inputs, a useful output artifact, and an explicit invocation point at the end of the process. Its result can be handed back directly as audit_evidence_bundle, and the persistence behavior has reuse value beyond this single sequence.
